title: LIVE SURFACE CURRENTS
source_name: NOAA/NOS Great Lakes Operational Forecast System (GLOFS: LSOFS/LMHOFS/LEOFS/LOOFS) surface-current nowcast + NOAA/GLERL experimental GLCFS-FVCOM Huron-Erie Corridor & lower St. Marys River nowcast fill
variable: u_eastward / v_northward surface-layer velocity components (filed m/s, direction of water motion TOWARD); speed = sqrt(U^2+V^2), displayed in cm/s; dense 1 px streamlets trace RK2 streamlines through the filed (U,V) field, micro-chevrons mark downstream direction
display_units: cm/s (speed gradient + streamlet brightness; chevrons show downstream direction)
coverage: Five Great Lakes + Mackinac Straits + upper St. Marys River (operational GLOFS) + St. Clair River / Lake St. Clair / Detroit River (experimental HEC FVCOM) + lower St. Marys River (experimental Michigan-Huron FVCOM). Narrow rivers restored product-locally where the shared open-lake shoreline mask reads land. Hard shoreline clip: land alpha is exactly 0. Documented gaps: St. Marys rapids/locks reach, Niagara Falls/gorge reach, other minor canals.
arrows: No preset lattice: thousands of 2 px streamlets trace RK2 streamlines (3 px steps,<=120 px paths) through the filed (U,V) field; brightness encodes speed (dim drift, bright jets); every second streamlet carries a tiny downstream chevron. All marks field-derived.
what: How fast the surface water is moving right now (color = speed, brighter streaks = faster) and which way it flows (thousands of fine flow streaks with tiny downstream chevrons). Covers all five Great Lakes plus the connecting rivers and channels where NOAA models provide current vectors.
why_extreme: Open-lake drift (a few cm/s, blue) owns most of the color resolution; river/channel jets to 100+ cm/s compress into red/dark-purple with the brightest streaks.
